standard.title: Develop inquiry questions
standard.description: develop questions to investigate a contemporary economic and business issue
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can develop questions to investigate a contemporary economic and business issue (AC9HE7S01). At Year 8, the expectation shifts toward questions that are more precisely targeted using economics and business concepts and terms, and toward a wider range of issue types.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop questions — including targeted questions using economics and business concepts and terms — to investigate a contemporary economic and business issue.

nodes.label: Broad and targeted question types
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish between broad inquiry questions and targeted questions that use economics and business concepts and terms, and explain why targeted questions produce more useful investigations.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one example of a broad question and one targeted question about the same economic or business issue; explain what makes the targeted question more useful for investigation.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a range of questions for an investigation — including broad framing questions and targeted questions using economics and business concepts and terms (e.g. 'How is the price of goods and services determined?' and 'Why do changes in market price act as a signal about how scarce resources should be allocated?'). Explain what each type of question contributes to the investigation.
wider: Compare the same economic issue investigated using only broad questions versus targeted concept-driven questions, and evaluate the difference in the depth and usefulness of evidence gathered

Practise converting everyday observations ('things are getting more expensive') into precise economic questions using specific concepts ('How does the relationship between supply and demand explain recent changes in housing rental prices in Australia?')
Investigate how professional economists and journalists frame questions differently about the same issue, and analyse what the different framings reveal about their purposes
nodes.hinge_reason: The distinction between broad and targeted questions determines the quality of all subsequent inquiry work — students who cannot frame targeted questions will produce unfocused investigations and struggle to locate relevant evidence in subsequent skill nodes.

response_modes.reason: The shift from 'why does X happen?' to a concept-anchored question requires understanding what economic concepts are available and what question type produces useful evidence. Explicit scaffolding — listing relevant concepts, then asking 'which concept does this issue involve?' — develops the targeting habit.

success_criteria: Develops at least one question using an economics or business concept or term accurately
Explains why a targeted concept-driven question is more useful for investigation than a broad question about the same issue

nodes.label: Developing a question set for investigation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can develop a range of questions — forming the basis of an investigation — that together enable systematic inquiry into a contemporary economic and business issue.
nodes.minimum_width: Develop at least two questions that together form the basis of an investigation into one contemporary economic or business issue — including at least one targeted concept-driven question.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a set of questions that form the basis of an investigation into a contemporary economic and business issue. The set should include framing questions (e.g. 'Why does X happen?'), targeted questions using economics and business concepts and terms, and questions about the issue's effects on different stakeholders.
wider: Develop question sets for two different types of economic issues (a market pricing issue and a business adaptation issue) and compare how the required question types differ
Evaluate a peer's question set against criteria: Are the questions investigable? Do they use concepts accurately? Do they lead to different types of evidence? Revise based on the evaluation
Investigate a real economic report or parliamentary inquiry submission and reverse-engineer the question set that appears to have driven the investigation

response_modes.reason: Question development improves through repeated practice across different issue types. Students benefit from developing question sets for multiple issues before the skill is assessed — each iteration adds to their repertoire of question patterns.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Question development is the entry point to all other inquiry skills. Students who practise across multiple issue types — market issues, business strategy issues, government policy issues — build transferable questioning capability that directly supports all subsequent skill descriptors.
success_criteria: Develops a set of at least two questions that together address different dimensions of a contemporary economic or business issue
At least one question accurately uses an economics or business concept or term as the basis for inquiry
